title: Gamma Fragility
one_line: Across a large panel of equity options, dealers' aggregate gamma imbalance shapes intraday returns: negative gamma → intraday momentum, positive gamma → intraday reversal, both stronger when the underlying is illiquid; gamma imbalance also relates to flash crashes.

findings.statement: Negative ex-ante dealer gamma → intraday momentum; positive → intraday reversal.
Effects stronger with higher illiquidity; strongest in the least liquid stocks.
Gamma imbalance linked to frequency and size of flash crashes.

why.pattern: Execution mechanics: dealers' delta hedging amplifies (short gamma) or dampens (long gamma) price moves.
why.mechanism: Short-gamma dealers buy rallies and sell drops; long-gamma dealers do the opposite.

reported_results.headline: Gamma sign decides momentum vs reversal.

tradable_edge: A regime switch for our momentum strategies: favour Noise Area / last-30-minute momentum when dealers are short gamma (proxy: after market drops / high volatility), and expect reversals when long gamma (quiet, rising markets).
angles: Gamma proxy (prior-day return < 0 or AvgRange above median) as a filter on momentum specs
data_fit: ES 1-min Dec 2013 → Sep 2026, NQ 1-min Jul 2021 → Sep 2026 (2024+ protected in the backtest project).
caveats: Abstract only; we have no dealer-gamma data, only proxies.
